column2: Here is the format used for measurement .csv files broken down to explain the intended use behind each of the sections within a .csv file
When a .csv document is in a VSCode work space with an appropriate tasks.json file, the comments made here following '
The .csv is run like normal python code through experimenter.py as a cartesian product of all possible variables within the list of parameters (param).
The cartesian product is run as a tensor product of all possible permutations
The appropriate syntax for functions and param can be observed below.

To run a .csv through experimenter.py, make sure to save your code ("ctrl" + "s") and press "ctrl" + "alt" + "s" to open the menu to run the code. Click run experimenter.py (or press enter if pinned) and the scan will begin running.
To track progress of a scan, the VSCode terminal is used as a log for machine activity.
A blank .csv can be made in your VSCode workspace where you have you device images and appropriate tasks.json file. All data will be saved there while scans are running.
Do not ever delete data after a scan starts. Shown below is when you can stop a scan and made edits and restart a measurement with new parameters.
If you make an edit while taking data, the procedure will not change but the data will no longer automatically populate.
To resume the data filling into the file, simply press "ctrl" + "s" and you will be prompted to compare to an alternate saved version.
Simply scroll down to the data that has been taken since the edit made and bring over to the new document version. Then click the check mark and the data should auto-populate again.
To stop a measurement process, kill the terminal by clicking the small trash can icon in the top right corner.
IMPORTANT NOTE: WHEN RUNNING THE MAGNET, IT IS ESSENTIAL THAT THE MAGNET RAMPING IS PAUSED. ONLY KILL THE SCAN WHEN THE MAGNET HAS REACHED A SET POINT OR IF THE MAGNET HAS PAUSED TO COOL DOWN
